estimated for each sample. --jeff

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Estimating density per point?
parts:
Eva:

My suspicion is that this will be very difficult. Unless you have
dozens of detections of each of your species at each of your points, you
will need to make some compromises. You may need to use global (pooled)
detection functions across points (or across species) to do what you
wish. However using these pooled detection functions in conjunction
with your point-specific counts will introduce dependencies between your
point-specific estimates. As such, you will not be able to make simple
comparisons of density between points because they are dependent because
of the shared detection function.

You might look at a similar question and answer by searching the
archives of the Distance-Sampling list (message 1417-1471 from 11 August
of this year.
